extraction.name: RoboFAC: A Comprehensive Framework for Robotic Failure Analysis and Correction
extraction.description: A paper introducing the RoboFAC dataset and model for robotic failure analysis and correction using video question answering over simulated and real-world manipulation failures.
extraction.creator: Weifeng Lu, Minghao Ye, Zewei Ye, Ruihan Tao, Shuo Yang, Bo Zhao
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed from simulated robotic manipulation tasks and real-world teleoperated robot executions. In simulation, expert policies were defined for tasks, failure trajectories were generated by replacing the expert policy with erroneous code snippets at selected substages, and videos were recorded with descriptive text. In the real world, data were collected via teleoperation using the SO-100 robotic arm, with each video paired with a textual description.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Experiments, Physical data collection, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The paper states that motion planning occasionally failed, producing trajectories that did not align with the corresponding textual descriptions; these were manually cleaned and approximately 75% of the collected data was retained.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Robot manipulation videos and trajectories from 14 simulated tasks in ManiSkill with objects from YCB Object Dataset and scenes from ReplicaCAD and AI2-THOR, plus 6 real-world teleoperated tasks collected with the SO-100 robotic arm.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Failure data were generated by replacing the original expert policy with a code snippet that produced an erroneous trajectory at a selected substage. For some failures, perturbed end-effector poses were recorded. The collected data were manually cleaned to remove trajectories that did not match the textual descriptions.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Manually cleaned the simulation data and retained approximately 75% of the collected data because some motion-planning-generated trajectories did not align with the textual descriptions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Raw videos and descriptions were annotated into video-based QA samples across eight question types. For task identification, task planning, failure detection, failure identification, and failure locating, reference answers were directly extracted from the textual descriptions. For failure explanation, high-level correction, and low-level correction, GPT-4o generated reference answers using the video and description, and all outputs were manually reviewed and corrected.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For five question types, answers were directly extracted from ground-truth textual descriptions. For the remaining three question types, GPT-4o-generated outputs were manually reviewed and corrected. The paper does not report inter-annotator disagreement or uncertainty analysis.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: One reference answer per QA item; five question types used direct extraction, and three question types used GPT-4o-generated answers with manual review.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The framework is intended to improve robotic failure recovery and assist VLA models in real-world manipulation, potentially increasing robustness and safety in robotic deployment.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that the dataset includes diverse backgrounds and camera viewpoints to improve visual diversity, but it also states that current robot failure datasets are limited and that the real-world evaluation remains subject to the VLA model's limited ability to follow complex natural language instructions.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The integration into the VLA-controlled robotic system is not yet seamless. The authors note that future work is needed for more natural and automated delivery of correction suggestions. They also note that the success rate remains subject to further improvement due to the VLA model's limited ability to follow complex natural language instructions.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, evaluation, and real-world deployment as an external critic for VLA-based robotic control; the paper also uses the dataset for testing and benchmarking multimodal models on task understanding, failure analysis, and failure correction.
